analysis: Reviewed three small ProviderLoop changes. (1) ProviderLoop+PrefetchPublication.swift head line 48 adds beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence(modelId) at publishVerifiedPrefetch entry, after the existing guards (selection revision, autopilot, revisionUpdatesInProgress). It is bookkeeping only. The weight-hash, self-test-record, retirement and CBv2-support guards that gate advertisement and the coordinator announcement are unchanged. The helper's definition is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not check that its per-occurrence state is cleaned up on every early return (e.g. the guards at head lines 54-69 and 88-115). A leak there would be a liveness or state-consistency issue, not a confidentiality one. (2) ProviderLoop+Preload.swift line 30 changes the load_model gate from autopilotAllowsModel to autopilotServesModel, and finishPreloadTask loses its private modifier (line 119) with no body change. The semantics of autopilotServesModel versus autopilotAllowsModel are not visible. If Serves is looser, the coordinator could trigger preloads of models outside the operator's autopilot selection. Eligibility, shutdown, revision-in-progress, draining and autopilotManagesResidency checks follow unchanged, and the coordinator is trusted for this push, so no concrete regression is evident. (3) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift adds a stop-request flag, a startupPreloadCandidate and transitionGenerations.begin(.startupPreload) for supervising a stalled preload driver. canLoadMore now also refuses new candidates when stop is requested, which makes it more restrictive, and the flag and candidate are reset on completion. No touch to A-001 plaintext handling, T-041 prefix-cache storage, attestation or authorization. Open questions for integration: the definitions of autopilotServesModel, beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence and transitionGenerations, and whether startupPreloadStopRequested is reset on all paths.
